first_step_test: One continuous head-and-body contour fixes the dove's left-facing flight direction, chest, back, and open attachment space for both wings without asking the learner to place disconnected parts.

source.notes: Planned six-panel handmade graphite contact sheet for the September 21 current lesson. Keep one left-facing dove, two fixed wings, one tail, one beak-held olive branch with seven leaves, restrained blue-gray and olive pencil, and no final-only structure. Preserve rejected iterations privately.

final_elements.name: head and body contour
final_elements.description: One continuous left-facing dove contour from rounded head through chest, belly, back, and neck, with reserved gaps for the wings.

final_elements.name: raised near wing and three tail feathers
final_elements.description: One broad wing attached high on the back and three tapered tail feathers joined at the rear body.

final_elements.name: lower far wing beak and eye
final_elements.description: One narrower far wing attached behind the lower body, one short beak, and one calm almond eye.

final_elements.name: olive branch with seven leaves
final_elements.description: One curved twig held at the beak tip with exactly seven alternating olive leaves.

final_elements.name: feather groups contour marks and broken shadow
final_elements.description: Five long near-wing feather divisions, three far-wing divisions, light body contour marks, and one broken shadow beneath the flight path.

final_elements.name: restrained blue gray olive and warm brown color
final_elements.description: Blue-gray pencil on the dove, olive green on seven leaves, warm brown on the twig, and cool graphite in the shadow.

frames.visible_job: Draw one continuous left-facing head-and-body contour, keeping a rounded chest, tapered rear body, and two clean wing attachment gaps.
frames.instruction: Start at the forehead, curve around the head into the breast and belly, taper toward the tail base, then return along the back to the neck. Leave one broad gap high on the back and a shorter gap beneath the body for the two wings.

frames.step_name: Lift the near wing and tail
frames.visible_job: Attach one broad raised wing at the upper gap and exactly three tapered tail feathers at the rear body.
frames.instruction: From the high back gap, sweep one broad wing upward and back, then return it to the same attachment with a shallow inner edge. At the rear body, fan exactly three tapered tail feathers from one shared base.
introduces: raised near wing and three tail feathers

frames.step_name: Add the far wing and face
frames.visible_job: Attach the narrower far wing beneath the body, then add one short beak and one calm almond eye.
frames.instruction: Use the lower reserved gap to attach one narrower wing sweeping down and right behind the body. Add one short pointed beak at the face and one small almond eye with its pupil aimed forward.
introduces: lower far wing beak and eye

frames.visible_job: Run one curved twig from the beak and attach exactly seven alternating olive leaves.
frames.instruction: Touch one slender curved twig to the beak tip and angle it down toward the lower left. Attach exactly seven narrow leaves in an alternating rhythm, keeping every stem joint visible and the first leaf clear of the dove's face.

frames.visible_job: Divide the established wings into feather groups, add sparse body contour marks and a broken shadow, then layer restrained blue-gray, olive, brown, and graphite.
frames.instruction: Pull five long feather divisions through the raised wing and three through the lower wing, following each wing's sweep. Add a few curved body marks and one broken shadow beneath the bird, then layer pale blue gray on the dove, olive on all seven leaves, warm brown on the twig, and cool graphite in the shadow.
introduces: feather groups contour marks and broken shadow
restrained blue gray olive and warm brown color

final_step.visible_job: Only deepen established contours, feather groups, restrained color, open-paper highlights, and the existing broken shadow.
final_step.instruction: Deepen selected chest, wing, tail, beak, eye, twig, and leaf edges with 2B graphite. Reinforce the established blue-gray, olive, and warm-brown pencil lightly, preserve the open highlights, and soften the same broken shadow without adding any new contour.

visual_review.first_step_observation: Step 1 is independently copyable: one clean continuous contour fixes the final left-facing head, chest, belly, back, and tail base while two obvious open gaps reserve the exact wing attachments.
visual_review.draw_through_observation: I inspected all six saved square crops pairwise at full size. The dove keeps one head-and-body silhouette, two fixed wing attachments, three tail feathers, one beak and eye, one beak-held twig, and exactly seven leaves. The repaired sheet removes premature color from Steps 1–4; Step 5 adds only the planned feather groups, body marks, shadow, and restrained color, and the finish only deepens those established regions.
